title: Shared progress, fidelity, degradation, and closure-evidence helper family
problemStatement: MCP runner and handler surfaces were manually constructing the same progress-event envelopes over and over, including phase transitions, streamed line forwarding, and ad hoc progress guards. That duplication risked subtle progress-shape drift across handlers and made runtime diagnostics less consistent.

duplicateClusters.name: MCP tool handlers building progress envelopes by hand
duplicateClusters.bestFix: Create one shared progress-event helper that owns start/done/progress/stream-line event emission so MCP handlers all publish the same event shape.

whyCurrentSharedModulesWereInsufficient: src/shared/progress.js is oriented around runtime logging, not context.progress event envelopes.
tools/mcp/runner.js had partial stream-forwarding logic, but the surrounding start/done event construction was still duplicated across handlers.

migrationsCompleted.notes: Now owns shared progress reporter and streamed line forwarding helpers.
Now uses shared progress-event helpers for runToolWithProgress.
Artifact-restore notifications now use the shared progress reporter.
Triage ingest/context-pack progress now uses the shared progress reporter.
Model download progress now uses the shared progress reporter.
Index build and heartbeat events now use the shared progress reporter.
Risk/context-pack analysis start and completion progress now uses the shared progress reporter.

nonGoals: Unify every fidelity or degraded-status contract in the repo in one pass.
Replace runtime logging helpers or observability envelopes.
Create a generic event framework for all surfaces.
followOnDeletionTargets: Continue hoisting other genuinely repeated progress/fidelity envelopes if later scans show the same tight seam outside MCP.
Leave specialized closure-evidence and fidelity-domain logic with their existing owners until a similarly narrow shared family is proven.
